text:
ash: heads-up - seeing slow steady memory growth on prod-gpu-*-pool (gk-23) since ~02:05 UTC. A few containers restarted with CUDA OOM around 02:10. Paging metrics for paged-attn spiked, KV cache free ratio dropping. not sure if it's allocator fragmentation or leak. kicking this thread to coordinate.
incident-bot: INCIDENT created: INC-2026-1859 - GPU node flapping / OOMs (sev:high) - paging observed - paging-alert rule fired
chris: ack. grabbing oncall. can you paste latest container logs and top output from the node? any customer errors yet?
ash: logs: 
```
2026-03-15T02:09:58Z runtime[pid=4128]: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
2026-03-15T02:10:02Z runtime[pid=4128]: container restart (OOM) - exit code 137
2026-03-15T02:11:05Z runtime[pid=4210]: kv allocator: slab split threshold hit, small fragments accumulating
``` 
kv stats snapshot (trimmed):
```
free_segments: 12345
avg_segment_size: 512
fragmented_ratio: 0.68
cache_entries: 12M
```
maya: that fragmented_ratio is the red flag. we've seen this pattern when paged-attention's allocator "small-slab" grows many tiny free segments and the overall bitmap ends up unusable -> slow OOM over hours. two mitigations we can run now:
1) disable paging on that pool to stop new paged allocations: `REDWOOD_KV_PAGING=0` (env) then restart runtime on affected nodes (rolling)
2) force a KV compaction on the workers (experimental) - `redwood-kvctl compact --pool prod-gpu-1 --aggressive` (this will pause inference briefly)
chris: plan: 1) throttle traffic off gk-23 (drain), 2) set REDWOOD_KV_PAGING=0 in node env and rolling-restart runtime on the pool, 3) run compact when node is drained. will do stepwise to avoid mass restarts.
ops-deploy-bot: rolling-drain initiated for node gk-23 by @chris. Command: `rwctl node drain gk-23 --timeout 10m` (progress updates will follow)
ryan: customer impact: support saw spike in 5xx for `embed` route starting 02:09 UTC. ~0.8% of prod requests failed over last 15m, two customers reported timeouts. CS tickets: #CS-1134, #CS-1135. alerted account owners.
ash: tagging affected models: rtx-large and rtx-quantized-8b; routing policy auto-fallback kicked in but capacity was thin so some requests hit OOM.
maya: quick safety change: reduce per-request max length to 1024 for that pool via runtime flag to reduce KV pressure: `MAX_SEQ_LEN=1024` applied in runtime config. doing that on warm pool now.
chris: applied `MAX_SEQ_LEN=1024` and `REDWOOD_KV_PAGING=0` to prod-gpu-1 (staged). rolling restart command:
```
for node in $(rwctl list-nodes --pool prod-gpu-1 --state ready); do
  rwctl node cordon $node
  rwctl node restart-runtime $node --grace 30s
done
```
logs during restart show one container restarted cleanly on gk-24; gk-23 drain in progress.
ops-deploy-bot: drain complete for gk-23. Node state -> drained. ready for restart.
maya: running `redwood-kvctl compact` on gk-23 now (low-risk because node drained). ETA ~ 90s. Output:
```
[compact] reclaimed 1.9GB, fragments reduced from 12.3k -> 3.4k
```
chris: after compaction, restarting runtime on gk-23 with `RD_RUNTIME_FLAGS=--kv-slab-threshold=2048` to avoid immediate re-fragmentation. bringing node back to service.
incident-bot: ALERT: node gk-23 rejoined pool prod-gpu-1 at 02:29 UTC
ryan: post-mitigation metrics: 5xx rate down to baseline, paging metric trending down. still monitoring for recurrence. customers notified that we're mitigating; follow-ups going to CS.
maya: follow-up actions (to capture in incident doc):
- create hotfix ticket for allocator to coalesce tiny free segments earlier
- add a guard to automatically disable KV paging when free ratio < 0.25
- add a compaction cron for high-fragmentation pools
- add extra observability: per-slab free histogram
chris: temporary mitigation checklist I ran:
- drained affected node
- disabled paging env var and reduced seq_len
- compacted KV store
- restarted runtime with higher slab threshold
- monitored traffic and verified error return to baseline
ash: handing over to chris for overnight oncall. summary below.

----- HANDOFF -----
ash -> chris
incident: INC-2026-1859
symptoms: slow memory creep via paged-attn allocator fragmentation leading to CUDA OOMs and container restarts; nodes flapped between 02:05-02:15 UTC; customer 5xx spike ~0.8%
what we did: drained nodes, disabled KV paging on pool, compacted KV store, set higher slab threshold, limited seq len, rolled nodes back in
current status: stable - error rates normalized, gk-23 back in service
next steps (owner: chris):
- watch fragmentation and paging metrics for 24h
- file allocator hotfix (tag: eng-runtime)
- schedule post-incident blameless RCA with eng-runtime + infra
- sync with CS on customer follow-ups
chris: taking it. I'll keep monitoring overnight and will escalate if we see >0.5% 5xx for 15m.
incident-bot: INC-2026-1859 status updated: monitoring -> mitigation. Primary assignee: chris. Pager quiet window set for 2h.
ash: thanks all. feel free to ping if anything pops up. :thumbsup:
